title: Reply: the church keeps written oracles — privilege is faith, not secret textbook knowledge
source_text: XXX. Respondeo, ut olim privilegium Judaeorum erat, quod ipsis eloquia Dei credita erant, ita quoque Ecclesiae Christianae privilegium est, quod ipsi commissa sunt eadem eloquia. Sed, ut Judaei illa scripto consignata habebant, ita quoque Ecclesiae Christianae scripto tradita sunt. Est ergo Ecclesia Scripturae sacrae & doctrinae coelestis in ea contentae, custos & depositaria. Quod si quam infideles ejus notitiam habent, ab Ecclesia illam mutantur. Deinde distinguenda est duplex mysteriorum divinorum notitia. Aliud est enim nosse quid Scriptura doceat, & quae sint religionis Christianae mysteria, & aliud ista mysteria credere, & certa fide amplecti: Potest enim aliquis in doctrina Christiana versatissimus esse & eruditissimus, qui tamen doctrinae Christianae non credat, sed occultam in corde tegat infidelitatem. Jam autem Ecclesiae Christianae privilegium proprie non consistit in priori illa notitia, quae non aliud est, quam simplex apprehensio illius quod dicitur, sed in illa notitia quae fidem quoque includit, & persuasionem certam illius, quod a mente nostra apprehenditur. Ut enim Alcoranum legere & discere possunt, neque tamen credant Mahumeto, & ejus Alcorano: Ita quoque Mahumetanus, & quilibet alius infidelis Scripturam legere potest, & totum Religionis Christianae corpus ediscere, neque tamen propterea religioni Christianae fidem adhibebit, & gaudebit privilegio fidelium, qui Christum & Evangelium ejus vere norunt & amplectuntur.
pass_a_gloss: I answer that as once it was the privilege of the Jews that the oracles of God were entrusted to them, so also it is the privilege of the Christian Church that the same oracles have been committed to her. But as the Jews had them sealed in writing, so also they have been handed to the Christian Church in writing. The Church is therefore the guardian and depositary of sacred Scripture and of the heavenly doctrine contained in it. And if unbelievers have any knowledge of it, they borrow it from the Church. Then a twofold knowledge of divine mysteries is to be distinguished. For it is one thing to know what Scripture teaches, and what the mysteries of the Christian religion are, and another to believe those mysteries and embrace them with certain faith: For someone can be most versed and most learned in Christian doctrine who nevertheless does not believe Christian doctrine, but covers a hidden unbelief in the heart. But now the privilege of the Christian Church properly does not consist in that former knowledge, which is nothing other than a simple apprehension of what is said, but in that knowledge which also includes faith, and a certain persuasion of that which is apprehended by our mind. For as they can read and learn the Koran, and yet not believe Muhammad and his Koran: so also a Muslim, and any other unbeliever, can read Scripture and learn the whole body of the Christian Religion, and yet will not for that reason give faith to the Christian religion, and enjoy the privilege of the faithful, who truly know and embrace Christ and his Gospel.
pass_b_english: Same privilege as Israel's: the oracles are committed to the church — and they came in writing.
She is guardian and depositary of Scripture; outsiders borrow knowledge from her.
Knowing the textbook is not believing the mysteries.
A Muslim can learn the whole Christian corpus without the faithful's privilege — just as one can read the Koran without believing Muhammad.
